method: Roots admitted by per-host review where neither the scan nor the APNIC probe could supply a verdict, each recording why review concluded what it did and why the other routes could not. This category exists because two evidence routes have a blind spot rather than because review outranks them - it is enumerated, small, and every entry states the limitation that put it here.

records.reason: ByteDance network-quality probe endpoint. Its clients measure against it to choose a CDN node, so the measurement has to traverse the path the media traffic uses; taken through a proxy it describes a path the client will not take and the client then picks the wrong node.
records.vendor_attribution: domain naming, and its use as the ByteDance probe by the split-tunnel test at ip.skk.moe that surfaced it
records.why_other_routes_failed: the apex does not resolve, and naming a mainland client subnet still returns foreign addresses for perfops1, perfops2 and perfops3 - 35.219.10.74, 95.40.53.40 and 47.84.187.31. Those endpoints are deliberately spread across regions because measuring only nearby would defeat their purpose, so hosting says nothing about how the traffic should be routed. byte-test.com, probed alongside it, does resolve into mainland space and is admitted on the APNIC route instead.
records.placement: china-web, alongside the ByteDance mainland infrastructure already there
